title: "Appendix B. Cumulative impacts of mining and wind power development on reindeer: landscape-scale habitat selection analysis (HSA)"
author: ""
#author: Bernardo B. Niebuhr, Erik Cronvall, Léonie Duris, Moudud Alam, Manuela Panzacchi, Bram van Moorter, Per Sandström, Anna Skarin
abstract: |
  Here we provide supplementary information regarding the landscape-scale (2nd order) assessment of reindeer selection for grazing sites in the Malå reindeer herding community, Sweden, under the presence of mining and wind power development, for the three snow-free seasons: calving, summer, and autumn. Taking into account different zone of influence (ZOI) radii for mining, different ZOI types (density vs. nearest) and radii for wind turbines, and different scales for the topographic position index, we fitted a total of 294 models for each season and compared them through model selection procedures. Here we present, for each season: (i) the setup of the habitat selection models; (ii) the best-ranged habitat selection models; (iii) the model selection tables comparing the structure and likelihood of the different models; (iv) the tables of coefficients; (v) figures illustrating the impacts of mining and wind turbines; (vi) maps with the predicted habitat suitability and GPS data across the three wind power development phases.

# Text B1: Statistical modeling of the HSA

As described in the main text, the landscape-scale HSA followed a habitat selection function
setup. The overall model structure we fitted was the following:

```{r}
base_formula <- case_ ~ 
  # habitat selection
  scale(dem) + I(scale(dem)^2) + scale(slope) + cos_aspect + 
  scale(sos) + 
  log(power_lines_dist+1) + log(priv_road_dist+1) + log(public_road_dist+1) + 
  log(trails_dist+1) + 
  log(house_dist+1) + 
  # mining habitat selection
  scale(mining_Krist_nearestXXX) +
  # wind habitat selection
  wf_name + 
  landcover*phase*scale(wind_turbines_ZZZ) +
  # tpi habitat selection
  tpi_scale_TTT
```

where the terms are:

- `case_`: our response variable (0/1);
- `dem`: elevation, we include a linear and a quadratic term; 
- `slope`: slope;
- `cos_aspect`: cosine of the aspect; 
- `tpi_scale_TTT`: topographic position index (TPI) computed at a certain scale, classified in 6 levels: flat, lower slope, medium slope, upper slope, ridge, valley;
- `sos`: start of season (used for calving and summer), replaced by `eos`, end of season, for autumn;
- `phase`: wind power development phase, with 3 categories: before construction, during construction, operation;
- `wf_name`: name of the wind power plant closest to each point, with four categories, added as a fixed effect to control for differential effects close to the Åmliden wind park, which lies along a large fenced area; 
- `landcover`: land cover, with 5 categories: deciduous forest, coniferous forest, open areas, mires, and anthropogenic areas;
- `log(public_road_dist+1)`, `log(priv_road_dist+1)`, `log(trails_dist+1)`, `log(house_dist+1)`, `log(power_lines_dist+1)`: logarithm of the distance to the nearest infrastructure for public roads, private roads, trails, houses, and power lines; 
- `mining_Krist_nearestXXX`: ZOI (exponential decay distance) of the mine, computed considering a certain ZOI radius; 
- `wind_turbines_ZZZ`: ZOI of wind turbines (considering either the density or the nearest infrastructure only), computed considering a certain ZOI radius.

The terms `XXX`, `ZZZ`, and `TTT` in the model structure above represent scales or variables that varied across models fitted. To evaluate the most likely ZOI for the mine and the wind turbines, whether there was a cumulative impact of multiple wind power plants, and at which scale the TPI most affected reindeer habitat selection, we replaced these variables in the model structure above using each possible combination of ZOI radii and type (cumulative vs. nearest; Fig. B1) for wind power and the different ZOI radii for the mine, together with different scales for the TPI. Models were compared through Akaike information criterion (AIC), as described in the main text. The scales included were:

- Mining (`XXX`): 100 m, 250 m, 500 m, 1 km, 2.5 km, 5 km, 10 km.
- Wind turbines (`ZZZ`): density of turbines or distance to the nearest turbine, with ZOI radii 100 m, 250 m, 500 m, 1 km, 2.5 km, 5 km, 10 km.
- TPI: 150 m, 250 m, 510 m.

All fixed terms are shared across models, and only the mine ZOI, the wind ZOI type and radius, and TPI scale varied. Consequently, all models had the same number of parameters (n = 49). This combination of possible variables resulted in a total of 294 models tested and compared for each season. Models were built with data of all individuals pooled.

![Figure B1. Illustration of two types of measures used to represent the influence of wind turbines in our study. The upper row shows the expected impact if we consider the effect of the nearest wind turbine only, which is similar whether one gets closer to one isolated turbine or a whole wind park. The bottom row shows the density of wind turbines, which captures the cumulative impact of multiple wind turbines and is larger when one gets closer to a wind park than to an isolated wind turbine. These two types of variables were used as predictors in the statistical models to estimate whether there were cumulative impacts of features of the same type.](FB1_conceptual_cumulative_impacts.png)

# Text B2: Best-ranked habitat selection models

This is the structure of the best-ranked HSA model selected for each season. 

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# calving
load("../../output/rsf_calving_multi_zoi_table_landcover_grouped.rda")
tab_models_calving <- tab_models |> dplyr::filter(!grepl("log", wind))
form_calving <- tab_models_calving$definition[1] |> 
  gsub(pattern = "\n   ", replacement = "")
# summer
load("../../output/rsf_summer_multi_zoi_table_landcover_grouped.rda")
tab_models_summer <- tab_models |> dplyr::filter(!grepl("log", wind))
form_summer <- tab_models_summer$definition[1] |> 
  gsub(pattern = "\n   ", replacement = "")
# autumn
load("../../output/rsf_results/rsf_autumn_multi_zoi_table_lc_grouped.rda")
tab_models_autumn <- tab_models |> dplyr::filter(!grepl("log", wind))
form_autumn <- tab_models_autumn$definition[1] |> 
  gsub(pattern = "\n   ", replacement = "")
```

Summary of best ranked models:

-   **Calving. Impact of the nearest wind turbine, ZOI radius = 5 km; ZOI of the mine with radius 10 km:** \
    `{r} paste(form_calving)`

-   **Summer. Cumulative impact of wind turbines, ZOI radius = 10 km; ZOI of the mine with radius 10 km:**\
    `{r} paste(form_summer)`

-   **Autumn. Impact of the nearest wind turbine, ZOI radius = 10 km; ZOI of the mine with radius 10 km:** \
    `{r} paste(form_autumn)`

# Table B1: Model selection table in calving

<!-- # Text B3: Model selection table in calving -->

<!-- Table B1 shows the ranking of most parsimonious models for 2nd order habitat selection -->
<!-- during calving. The best model for calving included the additive effect of mining at 10 km radius and  -->
<!-- of the zone of influence of the nearest wind turbine at 5 km radius.  -->
<!-- The second, third, and forth ranking models also included ZOI of the nearest wind turbine -->
<!-- at large scales, which does not include any support to the hypothesis of cumulative impacts of multiple  -->
<!-- wind turbines or parks during calving. All the best ranking models support a large ZOI radius for both the mine (10 km) and the wind turbines (5-10 km). -->

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (.is_pdf_output()) cat("Table B1 was truncated to show only the first 10 models, to avoid an overly long table. No models had a dAIC (difference in AIC) smaller than two from the best ranked model, and the first ommited model had dAIC = 252.20 in comparison with the best-ranked model.")
```

```{r aic_calving, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
#| label: aic_calving
#| fig-cap: "Table B1. Table of model selection for the HSA models for calving. Columns are zone of influence (ZOI) radius for mining and wind turbines, scale for the topographic position index (TPI), the log Likehood and AIC of the model, dAIC of each model in relation to the most parsimonious model, Akaike weights, cumulative Akaike weights, and the formula with each model's structure."

aic_calving <- readr::read_csv("../../output/rsf_results/rsf_calving_AIC_table_complete.csv")

aic_calving |> 
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("log", wind)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(dAIC = aic - min(aic),
                df = 49,
                logLik = round((aic - 2*df)/-2, 1),
                rel_likelihood = exp(-0.5 * dAIC),
                akaike_weights = rel_likelihood / sum(rel_likelihood),
                akaike_weights_text = ifelse(akaike_weights < 0.0001, "< 0.0001", akaike_weights),
                cumulative_akaike_weights = cumsum(akaike_weights),
                dAIC = round(dAIC - dAIC[1], digits = 2),
                aic = round(aic, digits = 2),
                tpi = sub("tpi_cat_s", "", tpi)) |> 
  dplyr::relocate(definition, .after = last_col()) |> 
  dplyr::relocate(logLik, .after = tpi) |> 
  dplyr::select(-c(lc, rel_likelihood, akaike_weights, df)) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Mining ZOI radius` = 1,
                `Wind turbine ZOI radius` = 2,
                TPI = tpi,
                AIC = aic,
                `Akaike weights` = akaike_weights_text,
                `Cumulative Akaike weights` = cumulative_akaike_weights,
                formula = definition) |> 
  # DT::datatable()
  make_table(truncate_lines_pdf = 10, col_widths = c("1.5cm", "1.5cm", "0.75cm", "1.2cm", "1cm", "1cm", "1.25cm", "1.15cm", "5.5cm"))
```

# Text B3: Disturbance effects on habitat selection

Here we present the coefficients of the HSA models. Even though all results come
from the same models, we split the way we present the parts of the resulting model, to ease
its interpretation. In this section we restrict ourselves on
presenting the coefficients of all infrastructure and landscape covariates, without going into 
details regarding the impact of wind turbines on habitat selection. 

In Table B4 we show the coefficient estimates for all the infrastructure types, excluding wind turbines which present interactions in the model structure and are explored further down. The estimates are put together for different seasons in Table B4 to make it easy to compare the effects between them.

A summary of the results:

- The mine was strongly avoided in all seasons, especially during calving, with a large ZOI radius of 10 km;
- Public roads were avoided in all seasons;
- Private roads and trails were avoided during calving and summer, but were selected in autumn;
- Power lines were avoided only during calving and were selected in the other seasons;
- Houses were avoided during autumn, but were select during calving and summer;
- Areas with a later start of season and a later end of season timing were selected during calving and autumn, respectively; in contrast, areas with an earlier start of seasons were selected during summer.

```{r coef_general, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
#| label: coef_general
#| fig-cap: "Table B4. Coefficient estimates for the infrastructure types and the start/end of season on habitat selection for all three seasons. The complete table of coefficient estimates for each season is shown in Tables B5, B7, and B9."
#| 
# read calving
coef_calving <- readr::read_csv("../../output/rsf_results/rsf_calving_coef_table_landcover_grouped.csv") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(significant = as.factor(if_else(p.value < 0.05, 1, 0)),
                p = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", round(p.value, 3)),
                select = case_when(
                  (estimate > 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate < 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "avoidance/negative",
                  (estimate < 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate > 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "selection/positive",
                  TRUE ~ "no effect"
                ))

# read summer
coef_summer <- readr::read_csv("../../output/rsf_results/rsf_summer_coef_table_log_lc_grouped.csv") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(significant = as.factor(if_else(p.value < 0.05, 1, 0)),
                p = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", round(p.value, 3)),
                select = case_when(
                  (estimate > 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate < 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "avoidance/negative",
                  (estimate < 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate > 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "selection/positive",
                  TRUE ~ "no effect"
                ))

# read autumn
coef_autumn <- readr::read_csv("../../output/rsf_results/rsf_autumn_coef_table_log_lc_grouped.csv") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(significant = as.factor(if_else(p.value < 0.05, 1, 0)),
                p = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", round(p.value, 3)),
                select = case_when(
                  (estimate > 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate < 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "avoidance/negative",
                  (estimate < 0 & grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) | (estimate > 0 & !grepl("log", term) & significant == 1) ~ "selection/positive",
                  TRUE ~ "no effect"
                ))

coef_all <- dplyr::tibble(season = c(rep("calving", nrow(coef_calving)), 
                          rep("summer", nrow(coef_summer)),
                          rep("autumn", nrow(coef_autumn)))) |> 
  cbind(
    dplyr::bind_rows(coef_calving, coef_summer, coef_autumn)) |> 
  dplyr::filter(grepl("log|nearest|sos|eos", term)) |> 
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("wind", term)) |> 
  dplyr::select(-c(statistic, significant, p.value)) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(term)

coef_all |> 
  # DT::datatable()
  make_table()
```

# Table B5: Coefficients - calving

```{r, echo=FALSE}

  dplyr::select(-c(statistic, significant, p.value)) |>
  # DT::datatable()
  make_table(col_widths = c("10cm", "1cm", "1cm", "1cm", "2.5cm"))
```

We also provide the table of variance inflation factor for the most parsimonious model. Note that all 
values in the last column are < 5.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}

  dplyr::rename("Term" = 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, digits = 2))) |>

```
